summary: The article surveys how local musicians use technology to create, distribute, perform, and learn music. It profiles artists using DAWs, mobile apps, direct-to-fan platforms, social media, cloud collaboration, and digital tools in education. It concludes that technology has become the cornerstone of local musical innovation.
one_line: Local artists use DAWs, mobile apps, streaming platforms, social media, and cloud tools to transform how music is made, shared, performed, and taught.
key_facts: Jamie Tiller showcased her new EP at the local arts center on October 14th, 2023; she produced it entirely in her makeshift bedroom studio using synthesizers and sampling in Ableton Live.
Jamie Tiller and Lina Rodriguez use software such as Ableton Live, FL Studio, and Logic Pro X.
Marcus Yi compiles field recordings into ambient tracks using GarageBand for iOS and Caustic 3 for Android.
In September 2023, Marcus Yi performed a live set with mobile apps at an open-air concert in Town Square Park, manipulating sounds in real-time.
Sara Beth, a local electronic producer, layers synthetic sounds with recorded vocals to create haunting melodies, as she shared in an interview on November 5th, 2023.
Folk singer Jason Miller released his latest album on Bandcamp and SoundCloud on December 1st, 2023, setting his own prices and retaining the majority of his profits.
DJ Emma Lopez blends turntable techniques with Serato DJ Pro, as seen at a downtown festival on December 15th, 2023.
Indie-pop singer Zoe Tran gained local fame through her YouTube channel, using backing tracks produced in Logic Pro X, and performed solo at the city's New Year's Eve celebration.
Martin Greene's YouTube tutorial channel saw a significant spike in subscribers after September 1st, teaching digital music creation and everything from music theory to audio processing.

In January 2024, local musicians Amy, Rohan, and Deepak released a triptych album, each contributing from their own home studio, with the final mix-down performed collaboratively in real-time through the cloud.
Local schools and independent workshops have begun integrating digital music creation into their curriculum.
Educator Susan Patel spoke at a seminar on February 28th, 2024, highlighting the importance of technological literacy in fostering the next generation of musicians.
